A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the practical models of surface loss are not as complex as those which have been developed in the literature, and that the practical models provide a useful description of the loss phenomena for the range of conditions for which the models have been tested.

a simple model for surface loss can be used for the purposes of transmission modelling, provided that the loss is applied to a deterministic description of surface shape, and provided that the loss model is adjusted to account for the presence of bubbles.

, for the conditions considered, the practical sub-models used by the authors are able to provide a reasonable representation of the surface loss phenomena, but that there remains a need to include a deterministic description of bubble formation and its effect on the sound speed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface loss values obtained with the sub-models are very close to the values from the small-slope model and the deterministic modelling.

, for mid-frequency and high-frequency applications, it is necessary to employ models which incorporate a deterministic description of surface roughness, in order to obtain surface loss values consistent with those obtained from the deterministic models.
